text:
A: Hi, erm, can you hear me? Sorry, I thought the last one was my last one, lol.
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Darren.
A: I'm Sana. I'm in Luton.
B: King's Lynn.
A: Oh, okay. Is that, erm, near Norwich?
B: Hour or so. West side of Norfolk. Near the Wash.
A: Right. Sorry, I'm rubbish with geography.
B: That's all right. Most people think Norfolk's just Norwich.
A: Lol. So what do you do?
B: Machine operator. Frozen veg factory. Twelve-hour shifts.
A: Twelve hours? That's like my partner. He's a delivery driver, he's out from like six in the morning, and this week the van's in the garage so he's had to borrow his cousin's, and it's just been, erm, a lot.
B: What's up with it?
A: Erm, I don't actually know. Something with the brakes? He said it was making a grinding noise.
B: Grinding's usually the pads worn down to the metal. If he left it, that'll have done the discs as well. Should be a couple of hundred for pads and discs. If they're quoting much more than that, he want to ask what else they're doing.
A: Oh, okay. They said like four hundred, I think.
B: Might be a calliper, then. Or they're having him on. Tell him to ask for the old parts back. Then you know they've actually done it.
A: Ask for the old parts back. Okay, I'm gonna tell him that. Do you, like, fix cars?
B: My own van. Brakes, oil, filters. I'm not paying someone sixty quid an hour to change a bulb.
A: That's fair. Imran can't even, erm, he can't even change a tyre, lol. Don't tell him I said that.
B: I won't.
A: So what do you do when you're not at work?
B: Fishing. Speedway on a Wednesday.
A: Speedway, is that like, motorbikes?
B: Yeah. Four riders, four laps, no brakes on the bikes. King's Lynn Stars. I've been going since I was a boy, with my dad.
A: No brakes? That sounds so scary.
B: That's the point of it. What about you?
A: Erm, I'm looking for work at the minute, nursery jobs, teaching assistant. My old nursery closed down. And I do mehndi for weddings, like henna.
B: Right. Any luck with the jobs?
A: Not yet. I check the sites every day. It's kind of stressful, not gonna lie. I feel bad, like, Imran's doing all these hours and I'm just at home.
B: You're looking, though. That's not sitting about. My dad was out of work when the Campbell's factory shut. He looked every day an' all. That's not on you if the place shut.
A: Yeah. Thank you. Sorry, I don't know why I said all that.
B: That's all right.
A: Do you have, erm, family near you?
B: My mum. Ten minutes away. I do her garden. She's got a hedge that grow faster than I can cut it.
A: My mum's ten minutes away as well! She rang me three times this morning about dinner.
B: Mine rings on my shift days to check I've eaten. I'm forty-five.
A: Lol, they never stop. Does she cook for you?
B: Sunday dinner, when the rota lines up. A roast. The rest of the time I do chilli in tubs.
A: Oh, I tried an air fryer thing yesterday and it was, like, a disaster. It was meant to be crispy chicken and it came out kind of
